skill.name: biomni
skill.description: Guides use of the Biomni biomedical AI agent framework for genomics, drug discovery, clinical genomics, molecular biology, and research workflow automation.
skill.summary: Use Biomni to plan and run biomedical research workflows with LLM-assisted analysis.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings in Markdown files are documentation examples, placeholder credentials, code fences, or public URLs and were adjudicated as false positives. Real risks remain in the setup helper because it collects and stores API keys, writes generated Python scripts, and executes a generated test script. Additional semantic review found full-privilege LLM-generated code execution and unescaped HTML report generation risks.

remediation.issue: The setup helper stores user API keys in a plaintext .env file and can print shell export lines containing secret values.
remediation.suggestion: Use an OS secret manager or provider-specific credential store, set restrictive file permissions, and redact secret values from terminal output.

remediation.issue: The setup helper interpolates a user-selected data path into generated Python files and executes the test file.
remediation.suggestion: Serialize dynamic values with repr or JSON encoding, validate paths, and ask for confirmation before executing any generated file.

remediation.issue: The skill documents Biomni code execution with full system privileges.
remediation.suggestion: Default to containerized or sandboxed execution, disable autonomous code execution for sensitive projects, and document least-privilege credential handling.

remediation.issue: The report generator converts conversation content to HTML without escaping user-controlled text.
remediation.suggestion: Escape HTML special characters, use a maintained Markdown renderer with sanitization, and strip scripts before writing shareable reports.

semantic_findings.title: Autonomous LLM Code Execution Runs With Full Privileges
semantic_findings.description: The skill states that Biomni executes LLM-generated code with full system privileges and advises isolation. This is an inherent high-risk behavior because generated analysis code can access files, networks, and credentials unless sandboxed.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The risk is explicitly documented in the skill text and is not just inferred from a code pattern.

semantic_findings.title: Generated Test Script Can Execute Unsafely Quoted Path Input
semantic_findings.description: The setup helper accepts a custom data path, embeds that value inside generated Python source, and then executes the generated test script. A crafted path containing quotes could alter the generated code before execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The data path is user controlled and is inserted into a single-quoted Python string before the generated file is run.

semantic_findings.title: Generated HTML Report Does Not Escape Conversation Content
semantic_findings.description: The report generator inserts conversation text into Markdown and later wraps lines in HTML tags without escaping content. Malicious conversation content could become active HTML in a generated report.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly appends message content and constructs HTML strings without an escaping or sanitization step.

content.user_title: Run Biomedical Research Workflows with Biomni
content.value_statement: Biomedical research tasks often require coordinated data retrieval, analysis code, and model configuration. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Biomni setup, task patterns, provider selection, and report generation.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to initialize the Biomni A1 agent with a data path and selected LLM provider.
Documents provider setup for Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Google Gemini, Groq, AWS Bedrock, and custom endpoints.
Provides task patterns for CRISPR screening, single-cell RNA-seq, ADMET prediction, GWAS analysis, and clinical genomics.
Includes an interactive setup script for conda checks, API key collection, data directory setup, and example script generation.
Includes a report generator that converts Biomni conversation histories into Markdown, HTML, or fallback HTML for PDF workflows.
Describes MCP configuration for connecting Biomni to external biomedical and search tools.
limitations: Requires the Biomni package, external provider accounts, and valid API keys before most workflows can run.
The Biomni data lake can require about 11GB of local storage on first use.
Biomni may execute LLM-generated code with full system privileges unless the user configures isolation.
Biomedical outputs require expert review and are not a substitute for clinical, regulatory, or laboratory judgment.

use_cases.title: Design Genomics Screens
use_cases.description: Plan CRISPR or single-cell analysis tasks with clear inputs, constraints, expected outputs, and reporting steps.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Drug Candidates
use_cases.description: Structure ADMET, target discovery, and compound prioritization prompts for Biomni-supported drug discovery workflows.

use_cases.title: Configure Research Agents
use_cases.description: Set up providers, data paths, MCP tools, timeouts, and reproducible report exports for shared research environments.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Gene Query
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple Biomni task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Biomni to answer a focused question about [gene]. Include molecular function, known disease associations, and key references to verify.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a CRISPR Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Biomni task for a CRISPR knockout screen studying [phenotype] in [cell type]. Include gene prioritization criteria, controls, expected analysis outputs, and safety constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Single-Cell Data
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate data analysis workflow using a local dataset.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide Biomni through analysis of [dataset path]. Perform quality control, clustering, cell type annotation, differential expression, and a concise interpretation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Provider Research Run
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with provider selection and reproducibility requirements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Biomni workflow for [research question] using [primary provider] with fallback to [secondary provider]. Define data inputs, timeout limits, validation checks, report outputs, and sandbox requirements.

output_examples.input: A researcher asks for a CRISPR screen plan for autophagy regulators in HEK293 cells.
output_examples.output: The skill should produce a structured workflow with candidate pathways, control design, sgRNA selection criteria, expected quality checks, and a review checklist.

output_examples.input: A platform engineer asks how to configure LLM providers for Biomni.
output_examples.output: The skill should compare provider options, required credentials, model choices, timeout settings, and safer storage practices for keys.

output_examples.input: A scientist asks for a reproducible report from Biomni conversation history.
output_examples.output: The skill should describe report inputs, supported output formats, metadata to include, and security checks before sharing generated files.

best_practices: Run Biomni in a container, virtual machine, or restricted environment before enabling autonomous code execution.
Use least-privilege API keys and keep biomedical datasets, credentials, and generated reports separated by project.
Specify organism, assay, dataset path, expected outputs, and validation criteria in every research prompt.
anti_patterns: Do not run Biomni against sensitive datasets on a host that also stores broad cloud or provider credentials.
Do not treat generated biomedical findings as validated clinical or laboratory decisions without expert review.
Do not share generated reports until they are checked for secrets, patient data, and unsafe embedded content.

faq.question: What is Biomni used for?
faq.answer: Biomni supports LLM-assisted biomedical research tasks such as genomics analysis, drug discovery, clinical genomics, and protocol planning.

faq.question: Does this skill include the Biomni package?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and helper scripts. Users still need to install Biomni and configure required provider credentials.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does Biomni require API keys?
faq.answer: Yes. Most workflows require at least one configured LLM provider key, such as Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Groq, Azure, or AWS Bedrock.

faq.question: Is Biomni safe for sensitive biomedical data?
faq.answer: Use caution. Run it in isolation, restrict credentials, review generated code, and confirm data handling rules before processing sensitive data.

faq.question: Can this replace expert biomedical review?
faq.answer: No. Biomni outputs should be reviewed by qualified experts before use in clinical, regulatory, or laboratory decisions.
